sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by fluorescent anti-Myc antibody staining of non-permeabilized transfected cells (PMC12337331) and by immunofluorescence in K562 cells (PMC4183217); no functional assay reported for the tagged constructs.
sites.rationale: L1 (PMC12337331) explicitly states the Myc tag was placed 'in the stalk region between EC6 and the transmembrane helix' of cPCDH constructs including PCDHA isoforms; L2 from the same paper confirms surface display by non-permeabilized staining. L3 and L4 (PMC4183217) independently corroborate the same stalk insertion for Pcdhα isoforms with surface localization confirmed in K562 cells. PCDHA13 is a PCDHA isoform and its stalk spans residues 660–697 (computed from the topology landmarks: extracellular ends at 697, TM begins at 698); no specific junction residue is named in any clip, so insert_after_residue is left null and the region is recorded. Two independent papers converge on the same region, giving high confidence that the stalk tolerates a short epitope tag. Two independent papers (PMC12337331 and PMC4183217) report insertion of an extracellular c-Myc tag into the stalk region between EC6 and the transmembrane helix of full-length, membrane-anchored clustered protocadherin constructs explicitly including PCDHA (alpha) isoforms. The constructs were expressed in transfected cells and the tag was placed in the extracellular stalk (PCDHA13 residues ~660–697, the 38-aa extracellular segment immediately N-terminal to the TM helix at 698). No specific junction residue is named in either paper.

sources.claim: For derived constructs including the Myc tag, the tag was positioned in the stalk region between EC6 and the transmembrane helix ( SI Appendix , Fig.

literature_notes: All four ledger clips (L1–L4) describe the same insertion modality — a c-Myc epitope tag in the extracellular stalk between EC6 and the TM helix of full-length membrane-anchored PCDHA constructs — from two independent publications (PMC12337331 and PMC4183217). Because both papers name the same region without specifying a junction residue, they support a single region-level site rather than two distinct residue-level sites. No N-terminal tag evidence is present in the ledger. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are named in any clip. The intracellular domain (residues 721–950) and the signal peptide (1–29) are not candidates for surface tagging and are not proposed.
